The fluorescent lights of the office hummed with the same energy as the panic rising in Dave’s chest. It was Bring Your Pet to Work Day, and Dave had made a catastrophic error in judgment. He had brought Barnaby, his African Grey parrot, not because he loved the bird, but because his wife was out of town and the pet sitter had canceled.

Barnaby sat perched on a stack of quarterly reports, his black eyes gleaming with malicious intelligence.

"Good morning, Dave!" chirped Barnaby, perfectly mimicking the voice of the CEO, Mr. Henderson.

Dave froze, his coffee cup halfway to his mouth. "Barnaby, hush," he whispered, glancing around. The open-plan office was quiet, save for the rhythmic clacking of keyboards.

"Quarterly earnings are down 15%," Barnaby continued, tilting his head. "And the CEO is embezzling funds through a shell company in the Caymans."

Dave dropped his coffee. It splashed across his shoes, but he didn’t care. He lunged for the birdcage, but Barnaby hopped to the top of the filing cabinet.

"Dave is wearing socks with sandals," Barnaby announced to the room.

Sarah from Accounting looked up, confused. "Dave, are you wearing socks with sandals?"

"No! It’s a joke! He’s mimicking!" Dave hissed, trying to cover the cage with a folder.

"Corporate espionage is a felony," Barnaby added, switching to the voice of the Head of Legal. "Also, Dave, you left the stove on at home."

Dave’s phone buzzed. It was his wife. He stared at it, terrified to answer. If he answered, Barnaby might mimic the conversation. If he didn’t, she might think he was ignoring her. He chose to ignore it, which was a mistake, because Barnaby picked up the slack.

"Dave is ignoring his wife because he’s afraid of her," Barnaby squawked.

Sarah stood up. "Dave? Is this true?"

"It’s not true! He’s a bird!" Dave yelled, finally grabbing the cage. He tried to carry it to the supply closet, but Barnaby was having none of it.

"Supply closet is full of expired yogurt!" Barnaby shouted.
